It runs "MiniMax H3" verified-with-caveats It runs OpenVDN's 8-step VDN-H3, a hybrid-attention derivative, not the stock dense H3 transformer. Results are those of that model. fields.hook: 49,134 dollars: two different accounts claim the same AI girl made it
fields.cta: Comment "90" for her list of red and green flags
fields.transcript: 49,134 dollars. That's the exact number that two completely different accounts are claiming to have made off of the same AI girl. Somebody's lying. Welcome back to my series where I'm testing AI money-making claims to see if they have real potential or if they are full of red flags. And hi, my name's Gianna. I'm trying to prove that I can make 100 grand in 90 days with the help of AI and everything that I build and learn I'm sharing with you for free so you can copy it step by step. You're going to want the algorithm to bring you back here so make sure to interact with this video and as many ways you can. I've been getting quite a few requests for AI-only fans content. You make that account go viral. You connect it to something called fan view and suddenly now you've made 50 grand. Except for both of those accounts are using the exact same screenshots and there are so many more videos doing the exact same thing. So fan view is a real platform and it does actually allow full AI-generated personas. But every single earnings figure attached to it actually traces back to someone who benefits from making money when you sign up for their fan view account. Meaning the people who are publishing these numbers are just getting paid for you to sign up under their link. I haven't been able to find any independent verification anywhere. Personally, this isn't an AI side hustle I really feel connected to so I'm not going to go that much deeper into it. But based on what I found already, I would probably say it's a red flag. For this challenge, I'm only building what I can actually verify and this one just does not pass the bar. Is it impossible to make money this way? I have no idea. But what I do know is every video that showing you just how easy this is, they're just copying the last one. I would move on. If you're interested in a real list of red flags and green flags that I've been researching and verifying, comment 90 and I will send them to you.
fields.screen: Two side-by-side screenshots of the same $49,134 earnings claim from different accounts, then the creator talking to camera with captions.
fields.summary: Part of a series testing AI money-making claims. She finds that the same screenshots appear across many videos, that Fanvue is a real platform that allows fully AI-generated personas, and that the earnings numbers come from people paid when viewers sign up under their link. She found no independent verification and advises moving on.
fields.research: Claim Verdict Evidence --- --- --- Fanvue is a real platform that allows fully AI-generated personas verified Fanvue is widely reported as allowing synthetic AI creators, e.g. Domus. Promoters earn from referrals, so earnings posts are biased verified Fanvue runs a creator referral programme, see its referral policy and Sirency's summary; terms differ between sources. Two accounts claim the same $49,134 with the same screenshots partly verified Shown on screen as two screenshots; the accounts' original posts were not independently opened. No independent verification of the earnings exists unverified The creator reports finding none; a search here also found no independent audit of these figures. Overall: Her method and conclusion are sound: the income screenshots are promotional and unverified.
fields.caveats: - She does not claim the model is impossible, only that the viral claims are unverified. - Referral terms vary between sources; check Fanvue's current policy. - Her own series is also a lead funnel (comment for a list). - Sells AI personas for adult-content platforms; check platform rules and local law before considering it.

fields.research: Claim Verdict Evidence --- --- --- Krea MCP can be added to Claude as a custom connector verified Krea's developer docs describe the hosted server at api.krea.ai/mcp, added via Claude's connectors with OAuth. Overall: The tool setup is real; the income claim is promotional and unsupported.
fields.caveats: - Tagged as a Krea partner post ( kreaaipartner), so it is a paid promotion. - Copying another channel's niche and style risks low-quality or reused content that YouTube may demonetise. - Comment-for-guide is lead generation. - Krea usage draws on a paid allowance.
